title: Piano Sonata No. 8 in C minor, “Pathétique”
hook: Heavy chords, a fast storm, and one of Beethoven’s best-loved slow tunes.

painting.title: The Death of Socrates
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A man meets death calmly, one hand raised, while his friends collapse in grief around him; the grave, noble pathos of the late 18th century that the sonata’s title names.

facts: Beethoven wrote it mostly in 1798, in his late twenties, when Vienna knew him above all as a fierce pianist. It was published at the end of 1799 and dedicated to Prince Karl Lichnowsky, one of his chief patrons.

The name is not a later nickname. The first edition was titled *Grande Sonate pathétique*, and the title most likely came from Beethoven himself. Apart from *Les Adieux*, the nicknames of his other sonatas, such as “Moonlight”, were added later by others. “Pathétique” means full of pathos: passionate and grave, not pitiful. The same word was later given to Tchaikovsky’s Sixth Symphony.
The slow, heavy opening does not stay at the door. It breaks back into the fast music twice. A reviewer noticed this as early as 1800.

It was a hit at once. In 1804 the ten-year-old Ignaz Moscheles, later a famous pianist, copied it out by hand from a library copy because he could not afford to buy it. His teacher warned him against such “eccentric” music.
bigPicture.inOneLine: thunder and flight (I), a song (II), a restless chase (III).

movements.heading: Grave – Allegro di molto e con brio
movements.tempo: Grave – Allegro di molto e con brio
movements.summary: A slow introduction of massive chords and sighs, then a fast, driving movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]. The slow music keeps coming back, and every return stops the storm in its tracks.

mainIdeas.name: The Grave
mainIdeas.description: a heavy chord struck hard that dies away at once, answered by soft, sighing chords in a jagged, dotted rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quick line climbing in the right hand over a rumbling left hand that shakes between two low notes an octave apart.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: one hand keeps a soft pulse of chords in the middle while the other leaps across it, picking out a melody now deep in the bass, now high in the treble, with little grace notes.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 3
mainIdeas.description: brighter, with quick rocking figures in both hands under a held high note.

stops.hear: A loud, dark chord that fades at once, then soft, sighing chords; the pattern climbs and grows
stops.happening: The Grave introduction

stops.hear: A run of tiny notes falls down the keyboard and the fast music bursts in: a low rumble in the left hand, a rising line in the right
stops.happening: Theme 1, over left-hand [[tremolo|tremolo]] octaves

stops.hear: Soft chords pulse in the middle while the other hand leaps over them, picking out single notes low and high, some with a little flick before them
stops.happening: Theme 2, in E-flat minor. A minor key here is unusual; a major key was expected

stops.hear: The mood brightens: a long high note over quick rocking figures, then a line that climbs in leaps
stops.happening: Theme 3, in E-flat major

stops.hear: The low rumble and rising line from ≈ 1:45 again
stops.happening: The [[exposition|exposition]] is repeated, from the start of the fast music

stops.hear: The fast music stops. The slow chords return, shorter, in a new key
stops.happening: The Grave breaks into the [[development|development]]

stops.hear: Fast again; short, clipped phrases wander through distant keys over the rumble
stops.happening: The development

stops.hear: The left hand hammers one low note; then the right hand, alone, runs all the way down the keyboard
stops.happening: A [[pedal-note|pedal note]] builds tension; the run leads home

stops.hear: The rumble and the rising line, back in C minor
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: Everything stops. The slow chords once more, quiet and hesitant
stops.happening: The Grave returns in the [[coda|coda]]

stops.hear: A few fast bars and hard, loud closing chords
stops.happening: The end

notice: Count the slow Grave music: at the start, before the development, and just before the end. Both returns are far shorter than the opening.
Listen to the left hand in the fast music. Its quick shaking between octaves is how one piano imitates a whole section of strings rumbling.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Barenboim takes the repeat of the exposition (≈ 3:45) and goes back to the start of the fast music, not to the slow introduction. Some pianists, András Schiff among them, repeat the introduction too.

movements.heading: Adagio cantabile
movements.summary: One of the best-known melodies Beethoven wrote, sung slowly in the middle of the keyboard. The movement is a simple [[rondo|rondo]]: the tune comes back three times, always in the same key, with two darker episodes between.

mainIdeas.name: The main melody
mainIdeas.description: calm and warm, in a low-middle register, like a voice.

mainIdeas.name: First episode
mainIdeas.description: a darker, more anxious melody in a minor key.

mainIdeas.name: Second episode
mainIdeas.description: a hushed minor-key section over a quicker, rippling accompaniment in groups of three.

stops.hear: A slow, singing melody in the middle of the keyboard; under it a soft, steady murmur of short notes and a low bass
stops.happening: The main theme, played [[cantabile|cantabile]]. One player, three layers

stops.hear: The same melody an octave higher, fuller and brighter
stops.happening: The theme repeated in a higher register

stops.hear: Darker; a new, more anxious melody in a minor key
stops.happening: The first episode, in F minor, moving to E-flat major

stops.hear: The main melody, back in its first, middle register, heard only once
stops.happening: The first return

stops.hear: Very quiet, in the minor; the murmur becomes a quicker ripple in threes
stops.happening: The second episode, in A-flat minor

stops.hear: Sudden loud accents; the music slips into a far-off key and finds its way back
stops.happening: A brief turn to E major

stops.hear: The main melody again, now carried on the rippling accompaniment from the episode
stops.happening: The last return. The tune is the same; what is under it has changed

stops.hear: Short phrases reach up high, then soft closing chords low in the piano
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: The melody never changes key. All three times it is in A-flat major. Listen instead to what happens underneath it.
The tune spends most of its time near middle C, the range of a cello or a tenor voice, not the bright top of the piano.

movements.heading: Rondo. Allegro
movements.summary: A quick, restless [[rondo|rondo]] back in C minor. The main tune keeps returning between brighter episodes, and the movement ends in a sudden, hard rush.

mainIdeas.name: The rondo theme
mainIdeas.description: a quick, nervous tune in the right hand over a light, rocking left hand.

mainIdeas.name: First episode
mainIdeas.description: a smoother, flowing tune in E-flat major.

mainIdeas.name: Middle episode
mainIdeas.description: slow-moving lines in several voices in A-flat major, almost like a hymn.

stops.hear: A quick, nervous tune in the right hand over a light, rocking bass
stops.happening: The rondo theme, in C minor

stops.hear: Brighter and smoother; then fast, cascading notes in threes
stops.happening: The first episode, in E-flat major

stops.hear: The nervous tune again
stops.happening: The rondo theme returns

stops.hear: Long, slow-moving notes in several voices at once, almost like a hymn
stops.happening: The middle episode, in A-flat major

stops.hear: The left hand pounds a low note; the right hand builds, then races down in loud runs
stops.happening: A [[pedal-note|pedal note]] leading back to the theme

stops.hear: The smooth tune from ≈ 0:33, now in C major
stops.happening: The first episode returns in a new key

stops.hear: The nervous tune for the last time
stops.happening: The final return, leading into the [[coda|coda]]

stops.hear: The music slows and softens; a fragment of the tune appears in a gentle major key, as if it might end in peace
stops.happening: A false calm in A-flat major

stops.hear: One last run down the keyboard and a hard, loud chord
stops.happening: The end, in C minor

notice: Listen to the quiet moment near ≈ 4:30. The tune turns gentle and major for a few seconds before the last run cuts it off.

threads.title: An orchestra in two hands
threads.body: Rumbling octaves like low strings, massive chords like a full orchestra, a singing line like a solo voice: one instrument plays every part.

threads.title: High and low
threads.body: The hands cross in the first movement, the slow tune moves up an octave in the second, and the finale’s last run tumbles from the top of the keyboard to the bottom.

threads.title: The pedal
threads.body: In the Adagio the [[sustain-pedal|sustain pedal]] lets the low notes keep ringing while the hands move on, which is how one player can hold three layers together.

threads.title: C minor
threads.body: Beethoven came back to this key for some of his most dramatic music, including the Fifth Symphony.
